messages.subject: Packrat does not fetch Bioconductor sources
messages.subject_clean: Packrat does not fetch Bioconductor sources
messages.body_plain:
Dear packrat developers and users, I'm hoping you might be able to provide some advice to a new user. I have just submitted a paper and am keen to use packrat for software version control in the interest of reproducibilty, i.e. to provide not only the analysis scripts, but also the exact same software that was used for the analysis. Packrat works admirably while I stick to the same platform and use binary library. But if I try to change the platform (i.e. from Linux to OS X) and have to use sources it fails at restoring the library. After some investigation I've noticed that my Bioconductor packages' sources are empty. To be exact, they are Not Found html pages. Here's the content: 404 Not Found

Not Found

The requested URL /src/contrib/Archive/BiocGenerics/BiocGenerics_0.14.0.tar.gz was not found on this server.

Apache/2.2.22 (Ubuntu) Server at cran.rstudio.com Port 80
I have seen the same behaviour on a Linux and OS X systems (see sessionInfo() at the end). Here's an example code that I've tried on both. mkdir new.project cd new.project R library(packrat) packrat::init() source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R") biocLite("BiocGenerics") packrat::snapshot() q() This seems to be only a issue with Bioconductor packages. CRAN packages are saved and restored as expected. Similarly, if I replace the Bioconductor sources with the manually downloaded ones, they restore as well. I'm wondering if there's some option I should be using to make sure that packrat fetches the source code from Bioconductor. OS X 10.6 sessionInfo R version 3.2.1 (2015-06-18) Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin10.8.0 (64-bit) Running under: OS X 10.6.8 (Snow Leopard) loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] tools_3.2.1 packrat_0.4.4-5 Linux sessionInfo R version 3.2.1 (2015-06-18) Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: CentOS release 6.4 (Final) other attached packages: [1] packrat_0.4.4-4 org.Mm.eg.db_3.1.2 RSQLite_1.0.0 Thanks!

messages.subject: Is it possible to use packrat with git repository?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to use packrat with git repository?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Could some one give me a pointer on how to use packrat in conjunction with git repository? It isn't clear to me in the documentation on the steps that I need to do.

Ideally, I would like to develop on a local machine (mac), push to a git repository (Bitbucket in my case, https://bitbucket.org/)
Pull on a remote machine (ubuntu) which will host my shiny app (digital ocean, thanks to Dean's tutorial, http://www.r-bloggers.com/how-to-get-your-very-own-rstudio-server-and-shiny-server-with-digitalocean/)

Thanks a million,

Iain

messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to use packrat with git repository?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to use packrat with git repository?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Iain,

For the most part, you should be able to use packrat and git 'orthogonally'. That is, just use git as you always would. The only thing you need to be aware of -- you should ensure that certain sub-folders in the 'packrat/' subdirectory are ignored.

For example, when I call 'packrat::init()' on a git-managed directory, a .gitignore file is generated with the contents:

    packrat/lib*/

which ensures that git won't try to track your installed packages (just the packrat lockfile, alongside package source tarballs).

Depending on your needs, you can also choose to ignore package sources by e.g. adding

    packrat/src/

as the source tarballs can take a large amount of space, but note that this implies anyone who wishes to restore your project after a git checkout will need to fetch the package sources from external repositories.

Hope this helps,
Kevin
